title: Meet in the middle
body: On sorted data, two pointers can shrink a search from both ends without checking every pair.
takeaway: Try two pointers when order lets one comparison move a boundary.

title: Reuse neighboring work
body: A sliding window updates one range by removing the outgoing value and adding the incoming one.
takeaway: Sliding windows avoid recomputing every overlapping range.

title: Process in arrival order
body: Which structure serves the oldest waiting request first?
takeaway: A queue is FIFO: first in, first out.

title: Find the shortest unweighted path
body: Which traversal finds the fewest-edge path in an unweighted graph?
takeaway: BFS explores level by level, so the first visit uses the fewest edges.

title: Go deep, then backtrack
body: Depth-first search follows one branch until it ends, then returns to try the next branch.
takeaway: DFS fits exhaustive search, connected components, and recursive structures.

title: Answer range sums quickly
body: After O(n) preprocessing, what is the lookup cost for a prefix-sum range query?
takeaway: Range sum left..right is prefix[right] minus prefix[left - 1].

title: What stops the calls?
body: A recursive function keeps overflowing the stack. What is most likely missing?
takeaway: Every recursive path needs to reach a base case.

title: Keep the top K
body: Which structure efficiently tracks the smallest item among the current top K?
takeaway: A size-K min-heap exposes the threshold in O(1) and updates in O(log K).

title: Measure a tree recursively
body: A node's height is one plus the larger height of its children.
takeaway: State the answer for one node in terms of smaller subtrees.

title: Why does graph search loop?
body: Traversal keeps revisiting the same cycle. What should be added?
takeaway: Mark nodes when discovered so cycles cannot enqueue them forever.
